title: Version scoring rules so older scores verify under their own rules
summary: The scorer has one RULES string, and the gate refuses or mis-recomputes any score written under older rules. PR #129's bound-only cost rule changed scores, so 8 older score files no longer recompute. I'll make the rules versioned: v1 keeps the old behavior, a new version holds the provisional-cost rule, and the gate recomputes each score under the version it records. No record is edited. The audience is the maintainer running `athena check --history` and CI.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the version dispatch; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Version the rules instead of special-casing the 8 files.
Only the versioning; no future-change gating.
Criteria run old-version and new-version scores through the gate.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Docs and changelog explain rule versions to outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: `athena check --history` passes on the full history, so PR #129's CI check goes green. The gate runs the scorer with the one current RULES string, so scores written before the bound-only cost rule cannot match.
Score files carry a `rules` string ending in 'v1' today (athena-score RULES). The new rule bumps the version to v2, and v1 is kept as an explicit, recomputable behavior.
I could not read the 8 score files because records/ is absent from my copy, so which exact rules string each carries is inferred.

I read athena-score/src/lib.rs, athena-gate/src/jobs.rs and history.rs. The producer should confirm the exact failing path (rules mismatch versus a recomputation difference) by running `athena check --history`.
The listed paths are inferred. Callers of score_records in athena-core, such as scoring.rs, may need a signature or version-argument update.
The existing rescore and re-score logic must also honor the recorded version.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. A new test recomputes a score that records the v1 rules string, using a killed or bound-only cost invocation, under v1. It matches the recorded score with the cost quantity not provisional, and the gate's job-record check accepts it.
Run `cargo test`. A test confirms a score written under the current rules still marks a bound-only cost provisional, and that the gate rejects a score whose rules string is not a known version.
Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. All pass.

The scorer defines each rule version explicitly: v1 keeps the pre-#129 behavior with no provisional cost for a bound, and the current version holds the bound-only rule. Each is selected by the rules string recorded in a score, and Score.rules is written from the version used.

The gate's job-record check in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs recomputes a score under the version it records and no longer demands equality with the latest RULES. An unknown version is still refused.
No file under records/ is modified, and the diff touches no athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow file. The change adds no gate that fails on future rule changes.
The change is documented in CHANGELOG.md and in the scoring or records docs: what a rules version is, and that older scores verify under their own version.

out_of_scope: Gating future rule changes on history, which the request calls a separate request
Showing provisional cost in the status display (display.rs)
The kill-switch reason coverage noted in job 60r4's findings
departures: The change touches the gate and the scorer, and I could not inspect the failing records. The cost and time are slightly above the reference.
